title: Qt: Do not spin new event loop on menu show
description:
There is no need for nesting event loops when showing menus. Show menus
asynchronously to limit possibilities of hard to debug problems related
to re-entering event loop.

notes.body: enabled an automatic merge when the pipeline for d1f7aa5acb2391a59111d5073e9bd9258a2154b6 succeeds

There is a difference between popup() and exec() that is not obvious at first glance. With exec, the menu exists throughout the execution of attached slots when an action is fired. With popup the Menu is cleared as soon as it is closed. This does not need to be a thing, but it could be. Especially if ->property or ->data is used for QAction or QMenu. 

Btw, exec is synchronous, popup is asynchronous. Meaning the event-loop is spun with the latter not with the former. But in any case, it is not really an issue for Qt, as it is run through the main loop anyhow. 

Also, I am not a huge fan of Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose. It was made popular by a few books in the beginning, but is a sign of not using Qt properly. If Qt is being used correctly, all parenting rights are being set. Therefore all objects are being deleted, once their parents are being deleted. Now in this case it is required as a workaround, because the context menus are being used as pointers, which they shouldn't be in the first place. 

A context menu should be a local variable, as it purely exists for the time the display time of the menu and the accompanying actions execution. As soon as that has been finished it is not needed anymore and removed from the context. Hence also the call to exec and the synchronous execution. As the menu is itself launched via the Signal/Slot mechanism, nothing is gained by making the menu a pointer and executing asynchronous. We are already in a different thread than the method which called the menu. Basically you start a sub-thread in a sub-thread with making it a pointer and calling popup. 

I am not saying this shouldn't be merged. If it solves a real world issue, for all means please do. All I am saying is, that there is a very good reason to avoid launching context menus via pointers and popup from the contextMenuEvents. And I personally think, this approach will not solve an issue but might cause new ones with the whole stacking of ->property and ->data elements.

The [stackoverflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/63714735/2200062) sums it up nicely. The issues caused by re-entered event loops are real and not obvious at all. See e7f5ba6aa7d6d56a7c375c02c911f61fc257d51f, ca1163ab60d85ae625d406b30c6eb31937bd1a1d for real world examples in Wireshark.

> Btw, exec is synchronous, popup is asynchronous. Meaning the event-loop is spun with the latter not with the former. But in any case, it is not really an issue for Qt, as it is run through the main loop anyhow.

What you wrote is incorrect. In fact the `exec()` does spin a new event loop, not `popup()`. Basically what `exec()` does is spinning `QEventLoop` and calling `popup()`.
